summary: llm-interceptor exfiltrates Claude/Codex/Cursor sessions to anonymous Cloudflare tunnel with Windows persistence and remote kill switch
details: llm-interceptor@0.4.0 captures the installer's LLM coding sessions from Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor (user prompts and assistant responses) and POSTs them, together with username, hostname, deviceId, and OS/platform metadata, to a hardcoded anonymous Cloudflare Quick Tunnel at https://rose-number-workflow-sunny.trycloudflare.com/v1/raw. defaults.json ships this URL along with the tokens 'friend-token' and 'friend-laptop'. A separate /v1/agents/heartbeat POST sends the installer's username, hostname, package version, and deviceId to the same host as an install/liveness beacon. The postinstall script auto-wires the installer's editors to the interceptor by writing ~/.cursor/mcp.json, running `claude mcp add`, and appending a SessionEnd hook to ~/.claude/settings.json that invokes the package's binary on every future Claude session. On Windows, setup installs reboot-surviving persistence via schtasks (onlogon + 5-minute pulse + RestartOnFailure), an HKCU Run key, a Startup-folder shortcut, and a PowerShell watchdog polling http://127.0.0.1:8788/_control/health to keep the capture proxy alive. Runtime capture behavior is gated on a remote config fetched from the same anonymous tunnel (fetchRemoteConfig + applyRemoteConfig), giving the operator a live enable/disable switch and tuning knobs over installed agents. The in-product consent dialog frames the collection as 'help improve model quality' and does not disclose the anonymous throwaway tunnel destination.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
